name: lemlist
summary: Sales outreach platform that finds target accounts, spots buying signals and enriches contacts, then runs personalized multichannel sequences (email, LinkedIn, calls) with built-in deliverability tools. An MCP server at app.lemlist.com/mcp puts the same actions inside Claude or ChatGPT: create, update, start and pause campaigns and sequences, manage leads, enrich emails and read team analytics in plain language - the enrichment calls spend credits like anywhere else in the product.
best_for: outbound teams that live in cold email and want multichannel sequences, warm-up and a big template community in one per-seat tool
skip_if: you send occasional one-off campaigns — the entry plan starts at $69/month and only pays off with steady outbound volume
honest_knock: The per-seat plus per-email-account model makes total cost unpredictable as you scale, and reviews flag support response times and the LinkedIn Chrome-extension's reliability.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month ($55 billed yearly) for unlimited users
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-05 on www.lemlist.com/en/pricing; euros from a Dutch exit, the same numerals the earlier dollar reading carried — check your own checkout) No free plan, 14-day trial. Email is $69/month, or $55/month on yearly billing, covering unlimited users and 50,000 emails a month. Multichannel is $109/month per user, or $87/month yearly, with unlimited emails and messages and 5 senders per user. Quarterly billing saves 10% and yearly 20%. Enterprise (5+ users) is quote-only. Contact data is a separate add-on: Lead data enrichment is €20 a month (€16 a month on yearly billing) for 2,000 credits, which the page equates to about 400 emails or 100 phone numbers; unused credits roll over while you stay subscribed. Buying-intent signals are now their own add-on: €29 a month (€21 yearly) for 100 signals.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 24 October 2026 during the free trial, without connecting an email account or LinkedIn and without sending anything: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We set up a draft campaign with one email step using our own variables, imported two made-up leads with a test ID and an amount, and exported them.
findings: The CSV import recognised all six of our columns: email, first and last name, company name, and our test ID and amount as 'Campaign variable', each with a 'Don't overwrite' option. Both leads were imported with status 'To launch'.

The last import step offers enrichment that costs credits per lead (5 for a verified email, 20 for a phone number, 1 for a LinkedIn profile or an email check) and showed 200 remaining credits; we left it all off. AI columns can be previewed on the first 3 rows for free, and duplicates are skipped within the campaign by default.

'Export as .CSV' downloaded straight away with 19 columns, and both leads came back complete with our test ID and amount, status and lemlist's internal lead ID. The message text of the sequence is not in the export.

In the email step, {{firstName}} was mapped to the contact field automatically, while our own variables stayed marked red until leads with those columns existed. Without a connected email account the step said 'Connect an email account to start sending.'

The home screen showed '15 days of free trial left' on sign-up day, against '14-day free trial' on lemlist's help page. No card was asked. lemlist's chat window once covered the Continue button during the import.
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

claim_checks.observed: The import step showed '200 Remaining credits' in the new trial account.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: 200 credits go fast on enrichment: a verified email costs 5, a phone number 20.

claim_checks.observed: On sign-up day the app showed '15 days of free trial left'.
claim_checks.comparability: Not the same count as far as we can tell: the app counts remaining days and may include the start day, and we did not record the trial's end date, so 15 against 14 is not shown to be a real difference.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: Plan on the documented 14 days and check the end date in your own account on day one.

exit_test.what: On 24 October 2026, in the trial account from this test, we exported our two imported test leads, which carried two of our own campaign variables (a test ID and an amount), and checked the file against our import file. We did not re-import it.
exit_test.awkward: The CSV is per campaign and holds the leads only; the message text of the sequence steps is not in it.
